propositions: The gate matches field names globally as bare attribute names rather than resolving reads to their owning dataclass, causing inert fields with reused names to pass silently when unrelated configs read those same names elsewhere

CodeHealthConfig.enabled had zero read sites but passed the gate because .enabled was read on UiConfig, McpConfig, and other unrelated configs, while CodeHealthConfig.analyzers required an explicit marker only because its name was globally unique

The gate newly flags four live fields (McpConfig.readonly, McpConfig.allow_llm, McpConfig.allow_jira_sync, JiraConfig.allow_insecure) when fixed to resolve reads to owning dataclasses, each read through documented indirection the old gate missed

The fix must implement receiver resolution through six patterns (section-attribute names, annotations, local aliases, return types, IfExp/BoolOp unions, cross-module call-site binding) so a read counts only when its receiver resolves to the field's declaring class
Each newly-flagged field receives a factual # read-via: marker naming its actual reader, never a silent exemption, following the existing pattern used by TrackerConfig.branch and VerifyConfig fields
